chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Razi who said:

A man wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the third: A man leased a property from a man, so the lessor sold that property which he had leased out in the presence of the lessee, and the lessee did not deny the sale, and he was present for it, a witness upon it. So the buyer died, and for him were inheritors, can they retract that in the inheritance or would it remain in the hand of the lessee up to the expiration of his term?
So he (peace be upon him) wrote: Up to the expiration of his term.
ai.seo_question: What happens to a lease if the landlord sells the property and then the buyer dies before the lease term ends?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali al-Rida (AS) establishes that the sale of leased land does not invalidate the existing lease, ensuring the lessee retains possession until the contract term concludes. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the buyer inherits the property subject to the existing leasehold rights, prioritizing the stability of contractual obligations over the heirs' desire for immediate possession.

en.hubeali: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq Al Razy who said,

‘A man wrote to Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 3<sup>rd</sup>, ‘A man leased a place from a man, so the lessor sold that place which he had leased out in the presence of the lessee, and the lessee did not deny the lessor of the sale, and he was present for it, a witness upon it. So the buyer died, and for him were inheritors, can they retract that in the inheritance or would it remain in the hand of the lessee up to the expiration of his term?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Up to the expiration of his term’.
en.sarwar: 3. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Raziy who has said the following:

“A man once wrote to abu al-Hassan, the third, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked about the case of a man who rented an asset from another man and the owner sold that asset in the presence of the tenant who did not raise any objection against the sale while he was present with witness and the buyer died; if the asset became of the legacy or remained in the hand of the tenant until the time of tenancy ended.
He (the Imam) wrote the answer that said, ‘It remains until the time of tenancy ends.’”
